title: Backend Developer
tagline: Design the APIs, databases and services that power every app.
about: Backend developers build what users never see: the servers, APIs, databases and background jobs behind every screen. You decide how data is stored, how requests are authenticated and how the system stays fast and correct under load.
It rewards careful thinking about data, failure and scale, and it's the foundation for later moves into distributed systems, DevOps or architecture.
day: Design and build REST or GraphQL APIs
Model data and write efficient SQL
Add authentication, validation and rate limits
Write tests and fix production bugs
Profile slow endpoints and add caching

phases.title: Programming foundations
phases.goal: Write small programs confidently and use the tools every developer uses daily.

nodes.d: Pick Python and get fluent with the basics before anything else. Fluency in one language transfers to every other.
links: CS50x: Harvard's intro to computer science

nodes.d: Developers live in the command line: navigating files, running programs and chaining tools together.
links: The Missing Semester of Your CS Education (MIT)
OverTheWire: Bandit (learn the shell by playing)

nodes.d: Version control is non-negotiable: every job uses it. Commit early, branch for experiments, open pull requests.
Break problems down, read errors calmly, use a debugger and print statements deliberately.
links: Exercism: practice in 70+ languages with mentoring

phases.title: Backend basics
phases.goal: Build your first API backed by a real database.

nodes.d: The protocol your APIs speak, and the conventions that make them predictable.
Use FastAPI (Python), Express (Node) or Go's net/http to route requests and return JSON.
Tables, keys, joins and transactions. Most backends live and die by their data model.
Connect, query safely with parameters, and manage schema changes with migrations.
Who are you, and what may you do? Sessions, tokens and permissions.
links: jwt.io introduction to JSON Web Tokens

nodes.d: Describe your API so others can use it, and generate clients.

project.d: A REST API with users, auth, CRUD for tasks, input validation, pagination, PostgreSQL, migrations and an OpenAPI spec. Add tests for every endpoint.

phases.title: Production backends
phases.goal: Make services fast, observable, tested and deployable.

nodes.d: Unit, integration and contract tests that let you change code without fear.
Avoid repeated work with Redis and HTTP caching, and handle invalidation.
Move slow work out of the request path.
Package your service and its dependencies identically everywhere.
Logs, metrics and traces so you can answer 'what is happening' in production.
The OWASP Top 10 from the server side.
Automate tests and deploys; ship small changes often.

project.d: A containerised service with Redis caching, rate limiting, analytics via a background worker, metrics and tracing, and a CI pipeline that deploys on merge.

phases.title: Scale & depth
phases.goal: Understand what happens when one server isn't enough.

nodes.d: Indexes, query plans and isolation levels: why a query is slow and how to fix it.
links: Use The Index, Luke: SQL indexing

nodes.d: Threads, async I/O and the bugs they cause.
links: Operating Systems: Three Easy Pieces (free book)

nodes.d: Network failures, replication, partitioning and consistency trade-offs.
Streams and message brokers decouple services.
Alternatives to REST and when they fit.
Design whole systems on a whiteboard: requirements, APIs, data, scaling and trade-offs.

project.t: Design and build a chat or feed service
project.d: A horizontally scalable service with WebSockets or fan-out, a message broker, read replicas and a load test report showing where it breaks.

interview: Design a REST API for a given product; justify status codes and pagination.
SQL: joins, aggregations, indexes and explaining a query plan.
System design: URL shortener, rate limiter, news feed, chat.
Concurrency: race conditions and how you'd prevent double-charging.
Medium algorithm problems: hash maps, two pointers, BFS/DFS.
